question: In 1690, the Dutch shifted their main headquarters on the Coromandel Coast from Pulicat to which of the following places?
explanation: The Dutch established their initial headquarters at Pulicat (Fort Geldria) in 1613, but shifted their administrative center of the Coromandel government to Negapatam (Nagapattinam) in 1690, which was closer to the southern trade routes and spice imports.

question: Under which treaty did the Dutch formally cede all their remaining factories and territories in India to the British, marking the end of their presence on the subcontinent?
explanation: The Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 (also known as the Treaty of London) officially resolved long-standing trade and territorial disputes between Great Britain and the Netherlands. Under this treaty, the Dutch ceded all their establishments in India (including Chinsurah and Cochin) and retired completely from the subcontinent, in exchange for the British ceding Bencoolen (Sumatra) and recognizing Dutch hegemony in Indonesia.
